newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom sees 96 oper profit at 7 bln marks - report.
newsitem.headline: Telekom sees 96 oper profit at 7 bln marks - report.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom expects its 1996 operating profit to rise by about three billion marks to seven billion marks, news magazine Der Spiegel reported, citing forecasts Telekom made to various banks.
Sales are expected to rise by five percent to about 62 billion marks, the magazine reported in an advance copy released at the weekend ahead of publication in Monday's editions.
Telekom, scheduled to go public in November in Germany's biggest-ever stock market flotation, will publish its half-year results on Tuesday.
Spiegel said Telekom's net profit in the full year will fall short of its 1995 net profit of 5.3 billion marks.
Chairman Ron Sommer had set aside 1.8 billion marks of the first-half net profit of 2.5 billion marks for the planned elimination of 60,000 jobs, the report said.
Telekom was expected to generate 1997 earnings of 10 billion marks or more and to pay out a high dividend, the report said.
Separately, a report in Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said there would be no delay in parliamentary discussions on Telekom's interconnection agreements with its competitors after its privatisation.
The postal committee of the German upper house of parliament last Wednesday postponed discussions on rules for the interconnection agreements.

But Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported that the Bundesrat, or upper house of the German parliament, would pass the interconnection agreement on September 27 as originally planned, rather than on October 18.

Earlier, Telekom said any delay would have no impact on the company's privatisation schedule. The only consequence would have been that the company's privatisation prospectus, due out early in October, would not have listed the interconnection clause of the law.
